name: Oracle average active sessions above CPU count
author: Sentra SOC
description: Average active sessions (V$SYSMETRIC, 60-second interval) above the instance CPU count (cpu_count) in 5 load-profile minutes within 5.5 minutes — the database is CPU-saturated or queueing; sessions wait for CPU or I/O. Tune: params.minutes = count, params.aas_per_cpu = the fields.aas_per_cpu threshold.

name: Oracle commit latency high (log file sync)
author: Sentra SOC
description: Average 'log file sync' wait above 10 ms with at least 1 commit wait per second in 3 of the last 5.5 minutes (V$SYSTEM_EVENT deltas) — commits are slow: redo log storage latency, too frequent commits or LGWR CPU starvation.

name: Oracle single-block read latency high (db file sequential read)
author: Sentra SOC
description: Average 'db file sequential read' wait above 20 ms with at least 1 read wait per second in 3 of the last 5.5 minutes — index / single-block I/O from storage is slow (SAN / disk latency or saturation).

name: Oracle session blocked for more than 5 minutes
author: Sentra SOC
description: A session has been waiting on a lock held by another session for 300 seconds or more (V$SESSION blocking chain: direct and final blocker, locked object). Typical causes: an uncommitted transaction left open, a hung batch job.

name: Oracle long-running query over 30 minutes
author: Sentra SOC
description: An active user call has been running for 30 minutes or more (V$SESSION last_call_et). The collector reports calls longer than LONG_QUERY_S (default 300 s); this rule alerts from 1800 s.

name: Oracle execution plan change: 2x slower
author: Sentra SOC
description: A statement switched to a new execution plan (new plan_hash_value in V$SQLSTATS) whose elapsed time per execution is at least 2x the best previous plan — typical after statistics gathering, an upgrade or a bind-peeking change. Consider a SQL plan baseline.

name: Oracle TEMP tablespace above 85 %
author: Sentra SOC
description: Temporary tablespace usage at 85 % or more (DBA_TABLESPACE_USAGE_METRICS; top consumer from V$TEMPSEG_USAGE) — sorts / hash joins will fail with ORA-01652 when it fills.

name: Oracle UNDO pressure / ORA-01555 risk
author: Sentra SOC
description: V$UNDOSTAT shows ORA-01555 (snapshot too old) or undo no-space errors in the last hour, or the longest query outlived the tuned undo retention while unexpired extents were stolen (fields.undo_risk = 1, reason in fields.undo_risk_reason).

name: Oracle processes or sessions above 90 % of limit
author: Sentra SOC
description: Current processes or sessions at 90 % or more of the configured limit (V$RESOURCE_LIMIT) — new connections will fail with ORA-00020 / ORA-00018 (connection storm, pool leak or a limit set too low).

name: Oracle tablespace forecast to fill within 14 days
author: Sentra SOC
description: Least-squares growth over the last 30 daily snapshots says the tablespace reaches its maximum size (including autoextend) in fewer than 14 days. SENTRA-ORA-009 covers a tablespace that is already 90 % full.

name: Oracle archive log destination error
author: Sentra SOC
description: An archive log destination (V$ARCHIVE_DEST) is in status ERROR / BAD PARAM or reports an error text — redo cannot be archived (local disk full, standby unreachable); the database hangs when all online logs need archiving. FRA usage is SENTRA-ORA-009, Data Guard lag SENTRA-ORA-010.

name: GoldenGate process aborted, disabled or in error
author: Sentra SOC
description: A GoldenGate integrated Extract (capture) or Replicat (apply) process reports ABORTED, DISABLED or an error in DBA_CAPTURE / DBA_APPLY - replication to the target has stopped and the copy falls behind from now on. Read the error, fix the cause, then restart the process from GoldenGate (GGSCI / Admin Client / Microservices).

name: GoldenGate replication lag over 30 minutes
author: Sentra SOC
description: A GoldenGate integrated Extract or Replicat is 30 minutes or more behind (capture message time / apply low watermark). The target copy is stale: check the process, the trail and the network, and the target database's apply performance.

name: Data Guard: redo not reaching a standby, archive gap or apply stopped
author: Sentra SOC
description: Seen from the primary (V$ARCHIVE_DEST_STATUS): a standby destination is in ERROR or reports an error, has an archive gap, or its redo apply is IDLE. Committed transactions are not protected on the standby. Read the error (network / listener / password file / standby disk), close the gap (FAL or restore the logs) or restart redo apply.

name: Data Guard: standby more than 30 minutes behind
author: Sentra SOC
description: A standby is 30 minutes or more behind: shipped logs waiting to be applied (primary side, V$ARCHIVED_LOG) or the standby's own apply / transport lag (V$DATAGUARD_STATS). A failover now would lose or have to wait for that much work.

name: Data Guard: redo apply not running or logs missing on the standby
author: Sentra SOC
description: On a standby: no MRP0 (managed recovery) process, or V$ARCHIVE_GAP lists missing archived logs. Redo is not being applied, so the standby is not current. Start redo apply (DGMGRL EDIT DATABASE ... SET STATE='APPLY-ON', or ALTER DATABASE RECOVER MANAGED STANDBY DATABASE DISCONNECT) and fetch the missing logs.

name: Data Guard: protection at risk on the primary
author: Sentra SOC
description: The primary of a Data Guard configuration runs with force logging off (NOLOGGING changes never reach the standby), a protection level below its configured mode, or a switchover status naming a gap or a failed destination.

name: Data Guard: fatal error or broker error
author: Sentra SOC
description: The database reported a Data Guard Error / Fatal message in the last hour (V$DATAGUARD_STATUS), or the broker reports an ORA- error for a member.

name: Database server: Oracle file system 95 % full
author: Sentra SOC
description: A file system on a server hosting an Oracle database is 95 % full or more (read over SSH by IT Asset Management). When the archive-log, datafile or diagnostic destination fills, the database stops (archiver stuck, ORA-00257) or cannot extend. Free space or extend the volume now.

name: Database server: instance down or host saturated
author: Sentra SOC
description: On a server hosting an Oracle database: an instance listed in oratab with autostart Y has no PMON process (the database is down on this host), memory available below 5 %, or load above 2 per CPU (read over SSH by IT Asset Management).

name: Database: mass delete, DROP or TRUNCATE on a followed schema
author: Sentra SOC
description: The Change Stream (LogMiner) saw a committed transaction that dropped or truncated a table, or changed at least the job's mass-change threshold of rows including deletes, in a schema it follows. Confirm it was an approved change; otherwise restore from backup / flashback.

name: Database: production data changed with an interactive tool
author: Sentra SOC
description: Rows in a followed schema were changed by an interactive client (sqlplus, SQL Developer, TOAD, DBeaver, ...) rather than the application. Usually a manual fix: check it against a change / incident ticket.

name: Replication or Change Stream stopped
author: Sentra SOC
description: The platform's own replication (a conflict, DDL on a replicated table, missing archived logs, a refused account) or the Change Stream (missing logs) stopped. The target / the audit stream is no longer current. The page says why; a person resumes it with a note.

name: Data Verify: source and target differ
author: Sentra SOC
description: A Data Verify comparison found rows missing, different or extra on the target after the in-flight re-check. A replica (GoldenGate, the platform's replication or a copy) has diverged: propose a repair from the page; a named DBA approves and runs it.
